theme: Woes to Ephraim and Judah; “in quietness and trust”
readingInstruction: Read Isaiah 28:1-30:33. These chapters are a series of woes aimed at the leaders of Israel and Judah. They are pointed and sometimes sarcastic. Look for the contrast between trusting in political schemes and “in quietness and trust.”
settingTheScene: As the Assyrian threat grows, the leaders in Jerusalem begin to look to Egypt for a military alliance. Isaiah condemns the plan as a covenant with death. The woes of these chapters describe drunken priests, hypocritical worship, secret plans made without God, and people who tell the prophets to stop giving them hard truths. At the center is a beautiful word about the cornerstone that God lays in Zion.
observation: “Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim” (28:1).
“Precept upon precept, precept upon precept, line upon line, line upon line, here a little, there a little” (28:10).
“You have said, We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have an agreement” (28:15).
“Behold, I am the one who has laid as a foundation in Zion, a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, of a sure foundation: Whoever believes will not be in haste” (28:16).
“This people draw near with their mouth and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me” (29:13).
“Woe to those who hide deep from the LORD their counsel” (29:15).
“In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and in trust shall be your strength. But you were unwilling” (30:15).
“Therefore the LORD waits to be gracious to you, and therefore he exalts himself to show mercy to you” (30:18).
interpretation:
Chapter 28 begins with the drunken leaders of the northern kingdom, whose fall is near. Then it turns to Jerusalem’s priests and prophets, who also stagger in drink. They mock Isaiah’s simple teaching as baby talk. “Precept upon precept” is how they hear it. God replies that if they will not listen to simple words, they will hear foreign tongues, the language of the Assyrian invaders.

The leaders have made a “covenant with death.” They think they have cheated the grave by political deals. But God lays a different foundation: a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, “a sure foundation.” Whoever believes in him will not be in a panic. The standard of justice will be the plumb line. In the face of political panic, the faithful rest on the stone God has laid.

Chapter 29 criticizes hollow religion. The people honor God with their lips but their hearts are far from him, and their fear of God is a tradition learned by rote. They think that God cannot see their schemes. Isaiah says the potter is not the same as the clay. God sees everything, and yet his plan includes a coming day when “the deaf shall hear the words of a book, and out of their gloom the eyes of the blind shall see.”

Chapter 30 is the center of this section. The people are sending envoys to Egypt, trusting in Pharaoh’s protection, and refusing to listen to the prophets. They say, “Do not prophesy to us what is right; speak to us smooth things.” God’s offer is simple: “In returning and rest you shall be saved; in quietness and in trust shall be your strength. But you were unwilling.” The most tragic words in the passage. Yet verse 18 is full of grace: “The LORD waits to be gracious to you.” The God who is angry is also the God who waits, and who will answer the cry for help.
connection: Peter quotes Isaiah 28:16 in 1 Peter 2:6 and calls Christ the cornerstone. Paul quotes it in Romans 9:33 and 10:11. Jesus quotes Isaiah 29:13 in Mark 7:6-7. Paul quotes Isaiah 29:14 in 1 Corinthians 1:19. Hebrews 4:9-11 speaks of a Sabbath rest for the people of God. Psalm 46:10 says, “Be still, and know that I am God.” Matthew 11:28 offers rest to the weary.
application:
Practice “quietness and trust” for ten minutes today. Turn off every distraction and simply rest in God.

Ask yourself where you have made a “covenant with death,” a plan to avoid consequences or guarantee security without God.

Receive the truth that the LORD waits to be gracious to you.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the cornerstone he laid.
Confess where you honor him with lips but not heart.
